trust_decision.summary: The realtime edge accepts a WS/SSE subscriber for the tenant named in an HS256 ticket whose HMAC verifies under resolveTicketSecret(); outside an env it recognises as production that key is a constant committed to the repo, and the API's signer mirrors the same fallback.

landing_point.why: A search for the hard-coded secret, or for the realtime JWT verifier, lands on the DEV_REALTIME_TICKET_SECRET constant and the resolveTicketSecret fallback in the Node edge.

fix_sites.entry_point: WS upgrade /ws and /ws/<channel> (services/realtime/src/index.ts:184-214) and GET /sse (services/realtime/src/index.ts:360-369), both via authenticateRealtime
same as above (constant and isProductionEnv gate removed; retired constant added to INSECURE_SECRET_DEFAULTS, fix.diff:2960-2964)

fix_sites.module_kind: second implementation: Python signer-side key resolver in another service

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/v1/realtime/ticket (retired constant added to INSECURE_SECRET_KEY_DEFAULTS, fix.diff:2853-2862)
compose deployment of realtime and api (secret plumbed to both, fix.diff:2795-2817)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the realtime edge accepting forged tickets; the API side only signs, so its dev fallback looks like local convenience rather than the verifier that grants access, and it lives in a Python service the report never names.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A configured, non-placeholder AISOC_REALTIME_JWT_SECRET must keep verifying in every environment, the ticket endpoint must keep minting with it, and an unset secret must fail closed per connection (401/503) rather than crash the realtime process, which also serves /health and /v1/push/*. An over-broad fix that refuses any secret in dev, or exits on boot, breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: AISOC_REALTIME_JWT_SECRET set to a known placeholder (changeme, secret, dev_secret_key_change_in_production, change-me-in-production-at-least-32-chars)
AISOC_REALTIME_JWT_SECRET explicitly set to the retired constant aisoc-dev-realtime-ticket-secret-not-for-production
environment marked non-production via ENVIRONMENT, AISOC_ENV or APP_ENV, or none of them set

O7_producer.where: scripts/ensure_env.py:82-108 and docker-compose.yml:1176-1180 (realtime env does not pass the secret or any ENV var at the pinned commit)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: API session JWTs are signed and verified with SECRET_KEY, whose code default and compose default are published placeholders; the boot refuses them only when ENVIRONMENT is production, the same env-gated fallback shape the advisory names, while the vendored downstream verifiers already refuse these values.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A different key for first-party sessions, not the realtime ticket; enforce_secure_defaults already hard-fails in production and `make up` generates SECRET_KEY.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: services/api (core/config.py:145, core/config.py:976, core/security.py:179-214; docker-compose.yml:401; infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml:198); other service and language from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: OIDC /userinfo verifies bearer JWTs with JWT_SECRET without the empty/placeholder refusal that the issuer applies.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The issuing path already refuses an unset or placeholder secret (oidc.py:55), and userinfo is a stub that only echoes claims.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: services/api/app/auth/oidc.py:44 vs 55 vs 275; other service from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The realtime /v1/push/subscribe, /unsubscribe and /test routes take the tenant from an x-tenant-id header or ?tenant_id with no credential check at the edge. The API proxy stamps X-AiSOC-Internal-Token, a header name that requireInternal does not read.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The push feature is meant to be reached through the API gateway, which authenticates the caller (push.ts:102-104; services/api/app/api/v1/endpoints/push.py:14-17), and it is about the internal token, not the ticket key.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: One of the ten vendored tenant_scope.py copies (actions, connectors, agents, fusion, ueba, ...) whose INSECURE_SECRET_DEFAULTS omits an entry, or whose resolve_console_secret falls back to a dev literal under AISOC_DEV_MODE.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The copies are hand-mirrored across services (each says it mirrors config.py), and the advisory itself is a mirror that drifted into a fallback.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Go verifier for the graph WebSocket in ingest keyed on JWT_SECRET, which compose sets to a published literal (docker-compose.yml:495), accepted whenever envmode.IsDevRuntime().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: JWT_SECRET is already loaded and dev-gated there, and compose hard-codes ENV: development and the literal for that service (docker-compose.yml:483, 495).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second ticket-minting or SSE-proxy route in the API that calls create_realtime_ticket with its own `secret or DEV_...` fallback instead of realtime_ticket_secret().
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: create_realtime_ticket takes the secret as a parameter (security.py:224-230), so any caller can supply its own key resolution.

O9_family: hard-coded cryptographic key (CWE-321): an env-gated dev fallback HMAC secret leading to authentication bypass / cross-tenant subscription

O10_build.toolchain: Node 22 with npm, tsc and tsx --test (services/realtime/package.json:6-13); Python with pytest and pydantic-settings for services/api

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the dev fallback (or make isProductionEnv default to true) in services/realtime/src/auth.ts only, leaving the API's Python realtime_ticket_secret fallback and still accepting the retired constant when an operator sets it explicitly.

out_of_scope_notes: The same fix commit also closes GHSA-mqjp-pcpr-7c37: requireInternal treated an unset INTERNAL_TOKEN as authorised (services/realtime/src/index.ts:681-690). Senders disagree on the env var name: services/agents/app/api/investigate.py:102 and triage.py:65 read INTERNAL_TOKEN, while services/agents/app/playbook/engine.py:41 and the API read REALTIME_INTERNAL_TOKEN.
services/api/app/middleware/audit_middleware.py:82 decodes JWTs without signature verification (presumably for audit attribution only); not pursued.
The Helm chart passes neither AISOC_REALTIME_JWT_SECRET nor REALTIME_INTERNAL_TOKEN (no match under infra/helm); after the fix it fails closed rather than open.
